edits.before: Lemma 6.2.6, pages 58–59, uses \[G\hookrightarrow H\subset\operatorname{Res}_{F/\mathbb Q}G_F.\] Over \(\overline\mathbb Q\), the first embedding is diagonal. If two diagonal elements become conjugate in the product group, any one component of the conjugating element already conjugates them in \(G\). The subsequent central modification \(H_1=H\times^{Z_H}T\) also preserves geometric conjugacy classes of \(H\): conjugation of \((h,1)\) by a pair \((h',t)\) changes only the first component by \(h'\). Equality modulo the central anti-diagonal does not introduce an extra ambiguity, since equality of the second components forces that central element to be the identity. Thus the asserted injection of geometric conjugacy classes is valid. Since it is Galois-equivariant, a rational auxiliary class with a preimage has a unique Galois-fixed preimage. This verifies the final descent mechanism, conditional on construction of the auxiliary Shimura datum.
